title: Record the SIGKILL clean-vs-dirty distinction in the repository profile, not in a Done record
description:
QCLI-271 is Done, and a completed record is an archive rather than a live operational fact. Its SIGKILL notes are the only place this repository states what the AMFI kill on npm/quest-darwin-arm64/bin/quest actually does, and they state it in the form it took in September, when the file was dirty mid-release: "any operation that makes git refresh/rebuild the full index" is killed.

Re-measured 2026-09-16 while answering opum-agent, who asked whether the kill still blocks the OPAG-114 recycle gate. It does not, and the reason is a distinction the Done notes do not draw:

  git hash-object npm/quest-darwin-arm64/bin/quest   -> exit 137, repeatable
  git status --porcelain                             -> exit 0
  git add -A --dry-run                               -> exit 0
  git diff HEAD --stat, git log                      -> exit 0
  git commit (real, 5 files)                         -> exit 0
  git cat-file -s <the stored blob>                  -> exit 0
  ./npm/quest-darwin-arm64/bin/quest --version       -> 0.7.1, exit 0, 3 of 3 runs

The kill fires only when git reads that files WORKING-TREE bytes and mmaps them, which is what trips AMFI page validation on a signed Mach-O whose pages are tainted. The file is currently clean and its stat matches the index, so nothing routine re-hashes it. The September behaviour was the same mechanism with the file DIRTY: a dirty entry forces a re-hash, so every index-refreshing command inherited the kill.

Stated as a rule rather than as a reading: the kill is armed by the files INDEX STATE, not by the repository or the volume. Leave the file clean and ordinary git works; make it dirty and the wide block returns. That is also why touching its mtime is not a harmless probe.

Worth writing down because the next person to ask will be asking during a release, which is the one time the file is legitimately dirty -- and the Done record will tell them the block is unconditional.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The repository profile in CLAUDE.md states that the AMFI SIGKILL on npm/quest-darwin-arm64/bin/quest is armed by the files index state -- clean means routine git works, dirty re-arms the wide block -- with the measured command list that distinguishes them

The entry names which operations were measured to still trip it (a working-tree content read such as git hash-object) and which do not (git status, git add --dry-run, git commit, git cat-file on the stored blob), so a reader can tell whether their own gate is affected without re-deriving it
The entry says it does not block a recycle gate that never re-hashes that path, and names the condition under which it would
QCLI-271s Done record is left unedited, since it is history and correct for the state it described

finalSummary:
Added "The AMFI SIGKILL on the darwin-arm64 binary is armed by INDEX STATE" to the repository profile in CLAUDE.md, immediately above the managed quest block (which is untouched and still last -- verified by line number after the insert, not assumed).

WHAT IT RECORDS. The kill fires only when git reads the working-tree bytes of npm/quest-darwin-arm64/bin/quest and mmaps them, tripping AMFI page validation on a signed Mach-O with tainted pages. The file is currently clean and its stat matches the index, so nothing routine re-hashes it. The September behaviour QCLI-271 documents -- "any operation that makes git refresh/rebuild the full index" -- is the same mechanism with the file DIRTY, where a dirty entry forces a re-hash and every index-refreshing command inherits the kill. Stated as the rule: clean means ordinary git works including a real commit, dirty re-arms the wide block, and touching the mtime is therefore not a harmless probe.

VERIFIED BY MEASUREMENT, not by reading the old notes. The command table in the entry is this sessions own output: git hash-object exits 137 repeatably, while git status --porcelain, git add -A --dry-run, git diff HEAD --stat, git log, a real five-file git commit, and git cat-file -s on the stored blob all exit 0, and the binary itself executes (0.7.1, exit 0, 3 of 3 runs).

WHY IT IS HERE AND NOT ON QCLI-271. QCLI-271 is Done. A completed record is an archive, and its notes are correct for the state they described -- so they are left unedited, which is criterion 4. The trap the entry names is that the next person to ask will most likely ask DURING a release, the one time the file is legitimately dirty, and the Done record would tell them the block is unconditional.

PROVENANCE. Re-measured while answering opum-agent, who asked whether this still blocks the OPAG-114 recycle gate. It does not, unless the gate re-hashes that path. They acknowledged and are recording the same distinction on OPAG-114, which narrows that tasks premise from a wall to a transient.

Gates: quest agents --check --require-installed --target claude exits 0 (state: current, skill state: current); lore check exits 0, 63 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings. No source changed, so bun run check was not re-run for this commit.
